note.p: Thomas James Alderson, son of Thomas Alderson (1740-1799), lived at Lower Eaton Street. His family connections include his grandfather, Rev James Aldrson (1727-1760). His parents were Thomas Alderson who married Sarah Boulby at Durham in 1789. Thomas Alderson’s siblings where Sarah born 1793, Durham, and Elizabeth born 1795 at Kirk Merrington, County Durham, who married in 1830 Henry Perronet Briggs (DNB 1791–1844). Thomas John Alderson himself was born 28 November 1791, Durham. Thomas John Alderson was articled to John Griffith, attorney of Common Pleas, in 1808. He was mentioned, not in a very good light, in a case at King's Bench 17 October 1827, Vice v Lady Anson (Standard 18 October 1827). He was declared bankrupt 27 June 1828 as money scrivener of Chancery Lane. In the 1851 census he was living at 10 Lancaster Place, Strand, listed as unmarried, and a clerk in the register office chancery. In 1863 his name appeared in newspaper ads as a director of the Constantinople and Alexandria Hotels Company Ltd. He died on 4 January 1864 at Lancaster Place. The Times of 29 January 1866 reported that the Company had been wound up without making any yield, leaving liabilities.
